guide.title: Project guide
guide.subtitle: Every screen, endpoint, tool and source of this profile, and how they connect.
guide.lead: The profile is one SQLite database behind one Nuxt process. The site, the REST API, MCP and the CLI are four ways to read and change the same data; this page is the map.

site.title: Site map
site.intro: Every route the app serves today: the main screens, the diagnostic log and the two system screens. The side nav groups the main ones and collapses to an icon rail; on narrow screens it becomes a drawer.

flow.title: How it connects
flow.intro: How a public source becomes a screen, and how a write from the browser, an agent or a terminal reaches SQLite and returns a diff with its journal event.

api.title: REST API
api.intro: The Nitro routes under /api, grouped by session, reads, writes and administration. Every mutation goes through the owning module and writes one event.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.intro: The MCP server exposes the same profile to an agent over stdio or HTTP: read tools, confirmed write tools and the same dry-run contract as the REST API. Virtual instances are not owned in game, yet they stay in read results and loadout previews.

cli.title: Commands
cli.intro: The npm scripts in package.json: develop and build, migrate and sync, inspect logs and verify the repository.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: The public origins behind the data, what each one updates and when it runs. Settings → Sources shows the same list with status and the last attempt; a failure keeps the old rows.

principles.title: Guarantees
principles.hint: Rules the code must not break
principles.intro: The owner-level rules the code must not break, and the tests that keep this page honest.

overview.title: Overview
overview.summary: The character sheet: identity, career numbers and the state of the data.

caps.profile: Nickname, faction, clan, clan rank and region; an absent faction reads as a missing value.
caps.kpis: Hours, K/D, accuracy and headshot share as the headline numbers; achievements, money, maximum money and the date the character entered the Zone below.
caps.edit: Edit identity fields and raw counters; clearing a counter restores the value from the API.
caps.freshness: Owned counts link to the four gear screens; the payload, price and catalog dates show how fresh the data is.

chat.title: Assistant
chat.summary: Threads with the in-app assistant; it reads through the MCP tools and acts through the same services.

caps.threads: Threads and messages persist in the profile database; the left pane switches threads, starts a new one and deletes one after a confirmation that removes its messages and files (audited, not rollbackable).
caps.tools: Read tools run freely and their results render as item rows, inventory tables and price lists, not raw JSON.
caps.confirm: A write first returns its dry-run diff and waits; Confirm runs it with the journal, Decline sends the refusal back to the model.
caps.model: The header switches the assistant model through the same audited setting Settings → Assistant uses; a provider without a list still accepts a typed id.
caps.background: A turn keeps running after leaving the page; its reply, pending write or error arrives as a toast, and returning reuses the stored thread.
caps.panel: A right-side panel on every page except /chat reuses the same conversation and composer; closing it never stops a turn.
caps.files: Images and text files attached to a message travel to the model with that turn; they live in the profile DB, are verified from their bytes, and are served only through the session. An image opens a carousel with thumbnails and zoom; a text file opens a readable preview with copy and download.
caps.streaming: Answers stream token by token; Stop aborts the provider call, and an incomplete answer is never saved. A turn that finishes while another page is open reports through a toast.
caps.reasoning: When the provider returns its reasoning, it sits in a collapsed block above the answer and can be expanded; it is stored with the message but never sent back to the model.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.summary: Equipment, the carried grid, stashes and the read-only intake stash, drawn like the game.

caps.equipment: A paper-doll of the ten equipment slots with level, rank and quality.
caps.grid: The left pane switches between the paper-doll and the selected stash, the carried grid stays on the right, and both are eight cells wide (the carried grid is 8×20, a stash 8×200); items move by drag and drop or with the keyboard: Space picks up, arrows move, Enter places and Escape cancels.
caps.stash: Stash tabs pick the left-pane stash — intake first, then the regular stashes; the storage manager creates and deletes stashes and changes their weight limit, and the wand packs items waiting in intake into the selected one.
caps.filter: Filter either grid by kind, rank and quality without moving anything; the matches repack from the top-left in the layout order, grid drops are refused while the filter is on, and clearing it restores every stored cell.
caps.tidy: Tidy repacks one storage in the chosen order (kind, name, rank or footprint); an item that cannot be placed stays at its cells and the toast reports how many stayed.
caps.intake: New and displaced items land in a read-only intake stash that only releases them and grows as it fills.
caps.loadout: Carry weight, protection, artifact effects and container warnings come from the computed loadout.
caps.form: The add and edit forms follow the kind: level and a matching skin for weapons/armor, one rarity percentage for artifacts, quantity for stacks; the slot is read from the catalog.
caps.virtual: An instance can be marked virtual (not owned in game): it keeps its grid cell, weight and loadout contribution, and every surface shows a dashed VIRT badge.

weapons.title: Weapons
weapons.summary: Catalog and owned weapons with damage, DPS and TTK at +15, plus each owned copy's level and location; a chart view compares damage falloff.

caps.catalog: Owned gear and the full catalog side by side; switch modes without leaving the page.

caps.filters: Search, type and rank filters, sorting, grouping and grid/list/chart views; the last view is restored per browser.
caps.manage: Add a copy from the catalog, edit level, quality or note, remove a copy; the item card opens from the row.
caps.falloff: Weapon modals chart damage by distance for the base and +15 levels, with axis ticks and a text list of every plotted point.
caps.chart: Chart view draws one damage-by-distance curve per weapon in the current list, colors each row, switches base/+15 and toggles series in the legend; the axis ends where the falloff does, and a fixed-height readout follows the crosshair with damage and TTK at that distance.
caps.target: Target HP sets the dummy's effective health for every TTK on the page; 600 is the default and reproduces the server numbers.

caps.manage: Add a modification from the catalog, remove an instance, or install it from a weapon's modification panel; the last filters and view stay in the browser.

flow.layersText: app/server → mcp → core → sources/shared. Lower layers never import upper ones; the app talks to the server only over HTTP.

sources.title: Public sources
sources.text: Adapters fetch and parse EXBO, the wiki, skins, prices, icons and the STALZONE profile. They never write to the database.

sync.title: Sync
sync.text: The sync module normalizes the responses, writes rows and records freshness. A failed source becomes stale; old data stays.

sqlite.title: SQLite
sqlite.text: One WAL database is the only source of truth. There is no second store, worker or cache.

core.title: Core modules
core.text: Each bounded context owns its tables; calc/ is the only place that produces DPS and TTK numbers.

clients.title: Consumers
clients.text: The payload read model feeds the Nuxt screens, the REST API, MCP and the CLI from the same rows.

entry.title: Entry point
entry.text: A form, an agent or a terminal calls the API, MCP or the CLI. Nothing writes SQL directly.

service.title: Write service
service.text: The owning module validates with zod, checks ownership and builds the before/after diff.

transaction.title: One transaction
transaction.text: The change and its event_log entry commit together; a dry run writes nothing.

result.title: Result
result.text: Callers get the dryRun flag, diff and eventId. Rollback restores the snapshot and logs a new event.

api.note: Every write accepts a dry run (dryRun in the body or dry_run in MCP) and returns the same dryRun, diff and eventId result. Mutations also require the matching Origin or a bearer token.

auth.login: Check the password and set the HttpOnly session cookie.
auth.me: Report whether the caller is signed in and when the session expires.

reads.healthz: Liveness probe for the process and the database.
reads.setup: First-run state: whether a character exists, catalog size and source status.
reads.payload: The whole profile in one response: character, gear, catalog, derived cards, icons and freshness.
reads.meta: Compact metadata: character update, catalog state and freshness.
reads.character: The character with its derived fields (K/D, accuracy, headshot, hours, arrival).
reads.items: Search the catalog by text, kind, rank and slot.
reads.item: One item with stats, effects, icon and the derived detail card.
reads.details: A derived card by key (w:, a:, art:, c:).
reads.inventory: The whole inventory: storages including intake, equipment and the loadout stats.
reads.inventoryItem: One inventory instance with its container artifacts or weapon modifications.
reads.containers: Containers with their current artifact fill.
reads.prices: Latest auction prices for a list of item names.
reads.sources: Source status, last success, last attempt and age.
reads.export: The typed profile JSON as a download.
reads.logs: Diagnostic log entries, newest first, with repeat groups.
reads.logsConfig: What the browser may capture: enabled, capture flag and effective levels.
reads.logsStats: Counts by level, category and source, storage size and process queue.

writes.characterCreate: Create the single character; a second create is rejected.
writes.characterPatch: Edit identity fields and raw counters; null clears an override.
writes.inventoryItemCreate: Add an item instance, optionally at a placement target; without one it lands in intake.
writes.inventoryItemPatch: Change level, quality, rarity, skin, note, role, slot, display name, quantity or a container override.
writes.inventoryItemDelete: Remove one quantity from a stack or the whole instance; children return to intake.
writes.inventoryItemMove: Move an item to a grid cell, equipment slot, container slot or modification slot; intake only releases items.
writes.storageCreate: Create an inventory (8×20) or stash (8×200) storage with an optional weight limit; system storages are rejected.
writes.storagePatch: Rename a stash, change its weight limit or its display order; system storages are rejected.
writes.storageDelete: Delete a stash and move its items to intake; system storages are rejected.
writes.storageAutoArrange: Pack intake items into a stash by first fit.
writes.storageTidy: Repack every item in one storage by the chosen order (kind, name, rank or footprint); an item that cannot be packed stays at its cells.
writes.containerFill: Replace a container's artifact fill from instance ids.
writes.weaponModification: Install, replace or remove a weapon modification; unknown compatibility needs an explicit unverified install.
writes.itemLayout: Override a catalog item's grid size and weight; a change that breaks placed items is rejected.
writes.rollback: Restore an entity from an event snapshot and log the rollback.
writes.logsPurge: Delete logs by filter or entirely; the journal event is not rollbackable.
writes.logsClient: Accept a browser error batch; each entry is validated, forced to client/client and rate-limited.

admin.cleanupRead: Count owned records, manual stats, the character and journal events.
admin.cleanup: Reset one scope: inventory, manual stats, character, journal or all; one journal entry keeps the snapshot.
admin.sync: Run a source sync; all covers catalog sources, profile stays opt-in.
admin.syncRead: Read source diagnostics and the auto-update schedule.
admin.syncSchedule: Update the auto-update schedule; one journal entry makes it rollbackable.
admin.loggingRead: Current logging settings and effective per-category levels.
admin.logging: Update logging: on/off, minimum level, retention, row cap and per-category levels.

chat.settingsRead: Assistant provider settings; reports whether the env key is present, never the key.
chat.settings: Update the assistant settings; one audited journal entry makes the change rollbackable.
chat.promptsRead: Active system prompt, skills and the composed prompt sent with a request.
chat.prompts: Append a prompt version and activate it; the previous pointer is rollbackable.
chat.threadRead: One thread with its ordered messages, including tool payloads.
chat.threadDelete: Delete one thread and its messages and files; the audited event is not rollbackable.
chat.turn: Run one assistant turn: reads execute, the first write returns its dry-run diff and waits for confirm.
chat.turnStream: Stream one assistant turn as server-sent events: the stored user message, provider text/reasoning deltas, tool phases, a pending write and one terminal done frame; aborting stores no partial answer.
chat.test: Send one model-list request to the configured provider and report its status.
chat.models: Reads the provider's model list for the settings picker; the key comes only from the named env variable and nothing is written.
chat.attachment: Bytes of one assistant attachment behind the session; images keep their sniffed type, text is served as plain text, sha256 is the ETag, and download/sandbox headers are always set.

policy.dryRun: dry_run defaults to true and returns the diff without touching the database.
policy.confirm: A real write needs dry_run: false and confirm: true.
policy.rate: At most 30 applied writes per minute per process.
policy.rebuild: rebuild_site does not rebuild anything; it reports the deploy command.

tools.get_inventory: Storages, equipment, the intake stash and the computed loadout.

tools.list_inventory_items: Inventory items filtered by kind, location or storage.

tools.get_prices: Latest auction prices by item name.

tools.remove_inventory_item: Remove an instance or part of a stack.
tools.move_inventory_item: Move an instance to a grid cell, slot, container or modification; intake only releases.
tools.create_storage: Create an inventory (8×20) or stash (8×200) storage.
tools.update_storage: Rename a stash, change its weight limit or its display order.
tools.delete_storage: Delete a stash; its items move to the intake stash.
tools.set_container_artifacts: Replace a container fill by instance ids.
tools.set_weapon_modification: Install or remove a weapon modification.
tools.set_item_layout: Change a catalog item grid size or weight.
tools.auto_arrange_storage: Pack intake items into a stash by first fit.
tools.sync_source: Run a source sync; requires confirm.
tools.rebuild_site: Reports the deploy command; MCP does not rebuild the site.
tools.list_logs: Diagnostic entries with filters, cursor and repeat groups.
tools.log_stats: Counts by level, category and source, storage size and queue state.
tools.get_logging: Current settings and effective per-category levels.
tools.update_logging: Change logging level, retention, cap and category overrides.
tools.clear_logs: Delete logs by filter or entirely; the journal entry is not rollbackable.

cli.note: These are the npm scripts of this repository; the canonical list is package.json and AGENTS.md.

commands.install: Install dependencies exactly as the lockfile pins them.
commands.reset: Delete the database file; check DB_PATH first.
commands.sync: Run source syncs from the terminal; add -- --force to bypass the price TTL.
commands.backup: Copy the SQLite file with the online backup API and prune copies older than 14 days.
commands.hashPassword: Print a scrypt hash for NUXT_PASSWORD_HASH.
commands.mcp: Run the MCP server over stdio against the local database or PROFILE_API_URL.
commands.smoke: Call every read tool against a temporary database and validate the shapes.
commands.testRelated: Run the test files related to changed sources.
commands.typecheck: Typecheck packages, server and the Nuxt app.
commands.typecheckNode: Typecheck packages and server without the slow Nuxt pass.
commands.boundaries: Check the dependency direction with dependency-cruiser.
commands.check: Typecheck, lint, boundaries and every test.
commands.golden: Compare the public fixture with the calculator baseline; expect 0 mismatches.
commands.logs: Print recent diagnostic logs; filter by level, category, text and time, or show --stats.

sources.note: all runs the five catalog sources. profile requires STALZONE credentials and never runs implicitly. Settings → Sources shows each source's status, last success and attempt, record counts where available, commit and origin; a failure marks it stale and keeps the previous data.

updates.exbo_base: Item identity and base stats from the EXBO database snapshot.
updates.wiki: Per-level damage, armor and artifact numbers, effect labels and container fields from stalzone.wiki.
updates.motifs: Skins and their base item links.
updates.scpmodel: Auction price quotes with a 15-minute TTL.
updates.icons: Icon files in ICONS_DIR and the icon rows that point to them.
updates.profile: Character statistics from the official STALZONE API (origin api).

triggers.catalog: Setup wizard, Settings (manual or scheduled), API sync or the CLI.
triggers.prices: The same sync path; inside the TTL it answers from the database.
triggers.profile: Only when explicitly requested and credentials are configured.

singleSource.title: One database, one process
singleSource.text: SQLite in WAL mode is the only source of truth. The site, API, MCP and CLI all read and write the same file; there is no second store or worker.

journal.title: Every write is reversible
journal.text: Each change commits together with an event_log row that holds before/after snapshots. Rollback restores the entity and logs itself.

numbers.title: No invented numbers
numbers.text: A missing lot, stat or price stays null and renders as “no lot” or “no data”. Zero, missing and estimated values never substitute for each other.

formula.title: One formula for DPS and TTK
formula.text: Every displayed damage number comes from catalog/calc/weapons.ts. Stored legacy display values are never substituted.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.text: No game credentials, no Steam or EXBO sign-in and no reading game files. Only public HTTP sources; the auction is read-only.

auth.title: Session and origin checks
auth.text: A scrypt password, an HttpOnly session cookie, a required Origin on mutations and a bearer token for /mcp.

keep.title: This page is part of the contract
keep.text: Adding or removing a screen, endpoint, MCP tool, CLI script or source requires updating this page. The test compares it with the code on every run.

forms.name: Name
forms.title: Title
forms.fillReplacesText: The existing artifact list will be replaced. Rollback is available in settings.
forms.layoutPairError: Enter both width and height, or leave both empty.

radio.error: The track could not be played.

logs.title: Diagnostic log
logs.subtitle: Server, MCP, CLI and browser events in one place. Fixes start here: filter to a level or request id, open an entry, and follow its stack.
logs.emptyText: Nothing matches these filters. Widen the window or lower the level; sync and MCP entries appear after they run.

purge.title: Delete logs
purge.text: Preview first: the diff reports how many entries the filter matches. Purging is audited but cannot be rolled back.
purge.note: A filtered purge keeps entries outside the filter. The audit event stays in the journal.
